subject: Helix PoC: model-fit + quantization evaluation roadmap
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Amelia Tan <amelia.tan@helixhealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 10 Apr 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Helix PoC: model-fit + quantization evaluation roadmap

Hi Amelia —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and a proposed plan to move from discovery -> actionable PoC work so we can validate model fit and quantify the throughput/quality trade-offs you asked about. High-level summary first, then concrete next steps.

Call summary (very high level):
- Primary goal: validate a small set of candidate models on your user queries (sensitivity, safety, and clinical accuracy) while meeting throughput targets for the web triage flow.
- Constraints: memory footprint for on-prem H100 pool, p95 latency target ~120ms, cost target ~$X/token (you gave ranges on the call), and strict PHI handling requirements (we'll route through Private).

Initial model candidates we recommend for the PoC (prioritized):
1) Llama-3-7B-instruct (baseline, high-quality FP16)
2) Redmond-7B-adapter (small adapter-tuned for clinical text)
3) mixtral-8x7B (good throughput/accuracy balance)

Quantization/throughput experiments (trade study focus):
- AWQ (aggressive int8-like quantization): lowest memory / best batching, may have subtle quality regressions on narrow clinical prompts.
- GPTQ (per-channel post-training quant): typically better quality than AWQ but higher memory/cost.
- FP8 (hardware FP8 on H100): minimal compute change, potential accuracy parity but hardware-dependent.

Concrete PoC plan (2-week rolling cadence):
Week 1 (data prep + baseline):
- Deliverable from Helix: representative prompt set + 1 week of anonymized web-triage logs (we only need ~2k examples to start).
- Internal: run FP16 baselines on Llama-3-7B and Redmond-7B. Metric: automated EM/ROUGE + safety filter rates.
Week 2 (quant trade study):
- Run AWQ and GPTQ pipelines on same eval set; run FP8 on H100 (if you give access or we run in Dedicated for you).
- Metrics: automated scores, top-1/regression diffs vs FP16, and targeted human review on 200 examples for clinical fidelity.

Owners & asks:
- Helix: share prompt set CSV (sample attached) and a small set of 50 golden examples for human review.
- Redwood (Marcus): run AWQ baseline + GPTQ runs and produce a short diff report.
- Redwood (Stephanie): schedule the benchmark runs and coordinate H100 vs A100 availability.
- Me (Neha): coordinate timelines, commercial terms, and consolidate results + next-step recommendations.

Attachments included: helix_prompt_samples.csv (sample prompt set), helix_eval_template.xlsx (scoring template). Also linking our eval templates here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1Helix-Redwood-EvalTemplates

Risks & mitigations (brief):
- Risk: AWQ may introduce subtle hallucination/regression on edge clinical prompts.
  Mitigation: human-in-the-loop review on 200 targeted cases and automatic regression thresholds.
- Risk: FP8 availability on your private infra.
  Mitigation: run FP8 in Redwood Dedicated for apples-to-apples comparison, fallback to FP16 if needed.

Proposed next steps (please reply with a preferred option):
A) Share prompt set + 50 golden examples by Mon 2027-04-12 -> kickoff Week 1 on Tue 2027-04-13.
B) If you prefer, we can run an initial small-shot eval on redwood-hosted infra first and share results before connecting to your private H100s.

If this looks good I’ll get Marcus and Stephanie to kick off the technical runbook and set a 30-min sync next week to review the results.

Thanks — looking forward to it.

Best,

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Helix PoC: model-fit + quantization evaluation roadmap

Neha — noted. Quick technical plan & acceptance criteria I’ll run once we have the prompt set: 

Plan (technical):
- Step A: baseline FP16 run on Llama-3-7B and Redmond-7B. Capture token-level logs, top-k outputs, and automated metrics (EM/ROUGE/F1).
- Step B: AWQ pipeline (our AWQ fork) -> produce quantized model + inference profiles (memory, latency across batch sizes).
- Step C: GPTQ (per-channel post-training quant) -> produce model + same inference profiles.
- Step D: FP8 run on H100 (if Helix grants access) to measure hardware FP8 performance. If not possible, run FP8-equivalent via Redwood Dedicated H100 and note environment differences.

Acceptance / regression thresholds:
- Auto-metrics: no more than 2% absolute drop on EM and F1 vs FP16 for primary clinical intents.
- Human review: <5% classified as "clinically unsafe/incorrect" on the 200-sample review.
- Latency: p95 <= 120ms for single-request with batching disabled (we’ll also report batched throughput).

Measurement details:
- We'll use the helix_eval_template.xlsx for structured scoring and keep the raw run logs in S3 (link to summary HTML will be shared).
- Human review will be blind and use a 3-rater majority on correctness + safety flags.

Notes on expected deltas (ballpark):
- AWQ: typically 1–3% automated metric regression vs FP16, with higher variance on rare clinical prompts.
- GPTQ: usually smaller regression (0–1.5%), but model size & memory trade-offs are worse than AWQ.
- FP8: when supported, often near FP16 parity on high-level metrics but depends on kernel maturity and mixed-precision path.

I’ll draft the runbook and attach the detailed protocol (awq-vs-gptq-protocol.md). Stephanie, can you confirm H100 slots for Thu/Fri this week?

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Sr. Applied ML Engineer | Redwood Inference
